import hashlib, json
from dspy.adapters.types.tool import ToolCalls, _canonicalize

TC = ToolCalls.ToolCall

# 1. basic: 64-char hex, id = first 8
tc = TC(name="search", args={"query": "hello"})
assert len(tc.fingerprint) == 64 and all(c in "0123456789abcdef" for c in tc.fingerprint), tc.fingerprint
assert tc.id == tc.fingerprint[:8] and len(tc.id) == 8

# 2. key order independence
tc2 = TC(name="search", args={"query": "hello"})
tc2b = ToolCalls.from_dict_list([{"name": "search", "args": {"z": 1, "a": {"y": 2, "x": 3}}}])[0]
tc2c = ToolCalls.from_dict_list([{"name": "search", "args": {"a": {"x": 3, "y": 2}, "z": 1}}])[0]
assert tc2b.fingerprint == tc2c.fingerprint
assert tc2.fingerprint == TC(name="search", args={"query": "hello"}).fingerprint

# 3. tuple -> list
assert TC(name="t", args={"v": (1, 2, 3)}).fingerprint == TC(name="t", args={"v": [1, 2, 3]}).fingerprint

# 4. string whitespace trimming
assert TC(name="s", args={"q": "  hi  "}).fingerprint == TC(name="s", args={"q": "hi"}).fingerprint
# but internal whitespace preserved
assert TC(name="s", args={"q": "h  i"}).fingerprint != TC(name="s", args={"q": "hi"}).fingerprint

# 5. name included in fingerprint
assert TC(name="a", args={}).fingerprint != TC(name="b", args={}).fingerprint

# 6. numbers/booleans preserved (no type coercion)
canon = _canonicalize({"b": True, "n": 1, "f": 1.5})
assert canon == {"b": True, "f": 1.5, "n": 1}
assert isinstance(canon["b"], bool) and isinstance(canon["n"], int) and isinstance(canon["f"], float)
assert TC(name="x", args={"b": True}).fingerprint != TC(name="x", args={"b": "true"}).fingerprint
assert TC(name="x", args={"b": 1}).fingerprint != TC(name="x", args={"b": True}).fingerprint  # json: 1 vs true

# 7. expected value check (recompute independently)
tc = TC(name="search", args={"query": "hello"})
expected = hashlib.sha256(json.dumps({"name": "search", "args": {"query": "hello"}}, sort_keys=True, separators=(",", ":")).encode()).hexdigest()
assert tc.fingerprint == expected, (tc.fingerprint, expected)

# 8. all construction paths
tc_a = TC(name="search", args={"query": "hello"})
tc_b = ToolCalls(tool_calls=[{"name": "search", "args": {"query": "hello"}}]).tool_calls[0]
tc_c = ToolCalls.model_validate({"tool_calls": [{"name": "search", "args": {"query": "hello"}}]}).tool_calls[0]
tc_d = ToolCalls(tool_calls=[TC(name="search", args={"query": "hello"})]).tool_calls[0]
assert tc_a.fingerprint == tc_b.fingerprint == tc_c.fingerprint == tc_d.fingerprint
assert tc_b.id and tc_c.id

# 9. fingerprint stable after args mutation (computed once at creation)
tc = TC(name="m", args={"a": 1})
fp = tc.fingerprint
tc.args["a"] = 999
assert tc.fingerprint == fp

# 10. explicitly provided fingerprint is kept
tc = TC(name="e", args={}, fingerprint="abc", id="abcd")
assert tc.fingerprint == "abc" and tc.id == "abcd"

# 11. format() unchanged
res = ToolCalls.from_dict_list([{"name": "search", "args": {"query": "hello"}}]).format()
assert res == [{"type": "tool_calls", "tool_calls": [{"type": "function", "function": {"name": "search", "arguments": {"query": "hello"}}}]}]

# 12. deep nesting
deep1 = {"a": [{"b": (1, "x ")}, "c"]}
deep2 = {"c": "c", "a": ["c", {"b": [1, "x"]}]}
assert TC(name="d", args=deep1).fingerprint == TC(name="d", args=deep2).fingerprint

# 13. None and empty values pass through
assert _canonicalize({"n": None, "l": [], "d": {}}) == {"d": {}, "l": [], "n": None}

print("ALL CHECKS PASSED")
EOF

python - <<'EOF'
from dspy.adapters.types.tool import ToolCalls, _canonicalize
TC = ToolCalls.ToolCall

# 12. deep nesting: same structure, different key order + tuple + whitespace
deep1 = {"a": [{"b": (1, "x ")}], "c": "hello"}
deep2 = {"c": "hello", "a": [{"b": [1, "x"]}]}
assert TC(name="d", args=deep1).fingerprint == TC(name="d", args=deep2).fingerprint

# list ORDER is semantic and must NOT be sorted
assert TC(name="d", args={"a": [1, 2]}).fingerprint != TC(name="d", args={"a": [2, 1]}).fingerprint

# 13. None and empty values pass through
assert _canonicalize({"n": None, "l": [], "d": {}}) == {"d": {}, "l": [], "n": None}

print("OK")
